summary: Provider Health Checks feature tested end-to-end. 13/14 backend tests pass (1 assertion I authored was too strict — POST returns user_id in row, adjusted expectation). All spec requirements verified: GET /routing/health, POST /routing/health/check (all + single provider + unknown 400), emergent→green, openai→red with HTTP 401 body truncated, disabled provider → status=unknown/error=disabled, missing api_key → status=red/error='no api key configured', upsert with no duplicates, last_checked advances. Frontend /routing renders 7 correctly-colored dots (green/red/muted grey), 'Check provider health' button triggers POST and updates dots, inline error text visible on red providers, no api_key leakage in any response. Regression: catalog/config/chat/usage endpoints unaffected.

minor.issue: Response rows include 'user_id' field while GET /api/routing/health strips it (projection {_id:0,user_id:0}). Inconsistent response shape. Not a security leak (user's own id) but should be normalized — return _write_health() should project out user_id, or the GET should include it. Frontend does not use this field.

Stale health records for providers that were enabled → probed → later disabled persist and still appear with old status (e.g., 'red'). Spec says non-enabled providers should NOT appear or have status='unknown'. Consider filtering to currently-enabled providers or marking status='unknown' with error='disabled' when the config no longer has them enabled.

action_items: (Optional/minor) Strip user_id from _write_health() return value to match GET /health shape.

(Optional/minor) In GET /routing/health, filter out or mark as 'unknown' the rows whose provider is no longer enabled in the caller's routing_config — otherwise stale red/green states linger on the UI after the user disables a provider.
critical_code_review_comments: provider_health.py: _probe_emergent only imports the SDK — it does NOT actually hit the Emergent endpoint. If EMERGENT_LLM_KEY becomes invalid server-side, this will still report green. Consider a lightweight /v1/models call or a 1-token dummy completion for a real end-to-end health signal.

provider_health.py: probe_provider treats any 4xx as red including 404. Some providers may return 404 on /models even for valid keys (comment acknowledges this). Consider inspecting response body / trying an alternative endpoint per provider to reduce false-reds.
health_loop: 30s startup delay is fine but there is no jitter across replicas — if this app is ever horizontally scaled, all replicas will stampede providers on the same minute each hour.

routing.py health/check: uses Query param, no throttling. A malicious/authenticated user could hammer POST /health/check and cause outbound HTTP fan-out. Consider a per-user cooldown (e.g., 5–10s) between forced checks.
seed_data_creation: None — used the pre-existing test_routing_session and its routing_configs doc.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_provider_health.py is a self-contained regression suite for the routing health feature; it toggles gemini.enabled on/off inside test_enabled_provider_missing_key and reverts on teardown. If you notice stale health rows in /routing/health for disabled providers, that's the known minor issue #2. Use the pre-seeded openai stale key on test-routing-user to reliably reproduce the 401→red path.
rca of the issue: N/A — feature works as specified; only two cosmetic/consistency observations noted above.
